attempts.summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, Alpine 3.23) from scratch, seeded application data (appdb.orders), then added node4 as a fourth member that received a full SST of existing data and now accepts writes like the others. Diagnosed and fixed an Alpine-specific bug where BusyBox's ps/lsof lack flags the wsrep_sst_rsync script depends on (causing false "SST daemon terminated unexpectedly" / infinite-loop failures) by installing the procps and lsof packages on all nodes. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id and cluster-health baselines, restarted each of the 4 nodes one at a time via native reboot (quorum preserved throughout since only one node was ever down), confirmed each node came back with a new boot_id, and verified MariaDB auto-started (rc-update default runlevel), rejoined the Galera cluster (wsrep_cluster_size=4, status=Primary, local_state=Synced), and retained/replicated all application data after every restart.
